title: Micro-Quickstarts sprint digest - standup notes
content:
Attendees: Aisha (owner), Marco, Fiona, Diego, Samira; skipped: Priya

Objective: rapid sync for the micro-quickstarts sprint (2-week cadence). Focus: ship 3 tiny quickstarts (Python, Node, cURL) + 2 sample notebooks and an onboarding checklist for new engineers/contributors. Keep this doc as the sprint digest — living notes, decisions, open items.

1) Quick wins completed since last check-in
- Python quickstart: basic generate flow done, README drafted, unit example passes. PR: sdk-quickstarts #82 (Marco). Needs CI flake check (see CI failures below).
- cURL example: minimal request + response cycle published to /examples/curl; tested against sandbox token.
- Onboarding checklist: first pass created, added to repo docs/ONBOARDING_MICRO.md (Fiona).

2) Blockers and triage items
- CI flakes on Windows runners for the Python example (intermittent). Action: Diego to open a smaller repro and add to INF ticket (JIRA-INF-2345). Priority: medium.
- Missing example for streaming responses: we decided to create a single combined streaming quickstart (Node + Python snippet) instead of separate ones to reduce maintenance. Action: Aisha to draft the streaming snippet by EOD Wed (2025-05-14).

3) New design decisions (consensus reached)
- Keep micro-quickstarts under a single repo (micro-quickstarts) not duplicated in sdk repo. Rationale: easier contribution surface and tiny PRs. Will add cross-link in each SDK README.
- Versioning: tag quickstarts with a date-style tag (e.g., 2025-05-14) rather than semver for now. Re-evaluate later if we see downstream dependencies.

4) Accessibility & docs polish notes
- Need alt-text and small screenshots for the cURL example (Samira). Add to checklist.
- Language: avoid deep inference jargon in quickstarts — aim for product engineers who just want to try the API. Fiona to do a language pass.

5) Action items (owner - due)
- Diego: create CI repro and attach logs to JIRA-INF-2345 (2025-05-16)
- Aisha: draft streaming snippet (Node & Python) + sample transcript (2025-05-14 EOD)
- Marco: fix unit test flake in PR #82 and re-run CI (2025-05-15)
- Samira: add screenshots + alt-text to cURL example and update ONBOARDING_MICRO.md (2025-05-18)
- Fiona: language polish pass, shorten copy for TL;DRs, update README headings (2025-05-18)
\n6) Follow-ups for Products/Docs/DevRel
- Docking with DevRel: want to have a 30-min walkthrough next week to align quickstart messaging with the "Get started in 5 minutes" flow on the docs site. Marco to propose times.
- Product: ask Hosted API team for an example prompt that shows graceful fallback behavior (to showcase rollback/fallback in quickstart). Aisha to ping the product channel.

7) Metrics we plan to track post-launch
- Repo stars / clones in first 30 days (rough proxy for adoption)
- Number of external contributors/PRs to micro-quickstarts in first 90 days
- Time-to-first-successful-request for a new user following the quickstart (aim: < 10 minutes)
- CI pass rate across OSes (target: >98% in CI after fixes)

8) CI / infra notes (technical)
- Current CI matrix: ubuntu-latest, macos-latest, windows-latest. Flake observed only on windows-latest (timeout on environment setup). Possible candidate: pip install using cached wheel to avoid long installs.
- Sandbox tokens: use the ephemeral token workflow documented in confluence (link above) rather than embedding keys in examples. Reminder added to README.

9) PRs / Issues to watch
- GH: micro-quickstarts #27 - discussion about placing notebooks under examples/notebooks vs docs/notebooks (strong opinion: examples/notebooks to keep repo focused). Vote: keep examples/notebooks (Aisha, Marco, Samira agree).
- GH: sdk-quickstarts #82 - Python quickstart (in review).
- JIRA-INF-2345 - CI flakes on Windows (blocking release).

10) Loose ideas / backlog (brainstorm fragments)
- "Mini-challenges": 3 tiny exercises in each quickstart so new users can verify they completed steps (badge-of-completion). Low effort, high UX win.
- Auto-generated troubleshooting FAQ: capture first 10 support questions and bake into README as troubleshooting section.
- Tiny sample dataset (500 tokens) to include in notebooks for deterministic behavior during demos. Consider privacy review.

11) Notes to self / informal snippets (copy these back to Confluence later)
- Keep examples tiny: 10-15 lines of code max per primary snippet. Secondary deeper-dive notebooks can be longer.
- For streaming example, show both SSE-style and SDK streaming callback pattern. Include expected partial outputs to explain streaming semantics.

12) Next standup (tentative)
- Date: 2025-05-21, 09:30 PT, 15 minutes. Agenda: CI status, streaming snippet review, DevRel walkthrough recap, PR merge plan.

Unresolved questions:
- Should we include a created-by header in each snippet linking to a person (e.g., "author: Marco Liu") or keep anonymous? Pros: accountability; cons: extra maintenance when people rotate. Defer decision until we see contribution flow.
- Do we want to include a small license header for sample datasets? Legal has previously asked for explicit tiny-license text. Tagging legal if needed.

Quick links (repeated):
- Repo issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/micro-quickstarts/issues/27
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-quickstarts/pull/82
- JIRA: JIRA-INF-2345
- Confluence: confluence.redwood.com/display/DEVEXP/Micro-Quickstarts
- Slack thread: https://slack.com/archives/C03ABCD123/p1621012345000

End of notes. Save this as the sprint digest for micro-quickstarts. Will copy key decisions to Confluence after merge of the first three PRs.
